summary: Masao Sekine (1912–2000) was a scholar in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1933–1936) and held a post at Tokyo University of Education (~1953–1976).
Masao Shizutani is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held assistant professor posts at Josai University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).
Masaru Akimoto is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyoto Women's University, including as professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society (attested 2002 and 2015).

Masashi Nagai (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (~1965–1969, PhD 1998). He held multiple posts at Komazawa, including professor emeritus (2017) and president (2019), and directed the Museum of Zen Culture and History.

Masataka Suzuki (born 1949) works in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Keio University (~1968–1978) and held a post there (~1980–2015), later serving as a lecturer at ICPBS and IIBS (attested 2026).

Masato Kobayashi (born 1970) specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1990–1995) and earned his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania (~1995–2000) under George Cardona, later serving as a research fellow at TUFS (~2000–2004).

Masatoshi Konishi (1938–2020) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at ICU, University of Calcutta, University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University, holding posts at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003).

Masatoshi Nagatomi (1926–2000) studied at Ryukoku, Kyoto, and Harvard University (PhD ~1953–1957 under Daniel H. H. Ingalls). A specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology, he held posts at Harvard University as instructor (1958) and professor (1969).

Masayuki Taira (born 1951) is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1978) and held posts at Osaka University (~1987–2017), Kansai University (~2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University.

Masayuki Tsukimoto (born 1952) specializes in Japanology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. He is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2026.

Massimo Pallottino (1909–1995) was an archaeologist and historian. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome (~1927–1931) and held academic posts at the University of Cagliari (~1940–1945) and Sapienza University of Rome (~1946–1980).

Masumi Mochizuki works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. Mochizuki held posts at Minobusan University as lecturer (attested 2001), professor (attested 2015), and special appointment professor (attested 2026).

Mathieu Boisvert (born 1963) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies who studied under A. K. Warder and Ravindra Panth. He became a professor at Université du Québec à Montréal in 1992.
Matteo Bartoli (1873–1946) was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (~1894–1898) and under Heinrich Hübschmann (~1898–1901). He held a post at the University of Turin (~1907–1946).

Matthew Orsborn works in Buddhist studies, earning a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under Guang Xing and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa. By 2026, he was attested as professor and Head of International Affairs at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Matthew R. Sayers is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under Joel P. Brereton and Patrick Olivelle. He held a post at Lebanon Valley College (attested 2013).

Matthew Steven Mitchell works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Osaka City University, the IUC, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and Duke University (PhD attested 2015 under Richard M. Jaffe).

Matthew T. Kapstein (born 1949) specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing a PhD at Brown University (1980–1987). He held posts at the University of Chicago, Columbia University (~1989–1996), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~2002–2018).
Matthew W. King is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Toronto (ending 2014) under the supervision of Frances Garrett.

Matthias Alexander Castrén (1813–1852) specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Helsinki / Imperial Alexander University (~1830–1836) and held a post there from ~1840 to 1852.
